Mbah described the death as a personal loss to Enugu State, recalling that although the renowned actor hailed from Nteje in Anambra State, he had consistently acknowledged his longstanding ties with Enugu, which he often described as his birthplace, first port of call and home away from home. The governor, in a personal tribute issued in the early hours of Wednesday following the announcement of the actor’s death by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, also described the deceased as a great ambassador of Enugu State and a supporter of his administration. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Chief Pete Edochie, one of Nigeria’s most iconic actors and titans, and one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood and Africa’s creative industry across the world,” Mbah said. He noted that the death came at a particularly significant time when Enugu was hosting the National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST), describing the development as a painful loss to the state’s cultural community. The governor said the actor’s contribution to the creative industry went beyond entertainment, noting that his performances helped preserve Nigerian cultural values and project the country’s heritage to international audiences. “Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor; he was an institution. With his commanding screen presence, unmistakable voice, remarkable mastery of dialogue and profound understanding of his craft, he helped shape the identity of Nigerian cinema and took the stories, values and cultural expressions of our people to audiences across the world,” he said. Mbah recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s 1958 novel, Things Fall Apart, saying the role helped communicate Igbo culture and Nigerian society to the world. He said the actor proudly promoted his Igbo identity through his use of the language, proverbs, wisdom and cultural traditions, inspiring generations of actors and storytellers. According to him, Edochie’s career was defined by excellence, distinction, longevity and uncommon social grace, adding that his legacy as a broadcaster, actor and cultural ambassador would endure. The governor said the actor’s death was particularly painful for the people of Enugu, while extending condolences to his immediate family, the Nollywood community, the Anambra State Government and Nigerians across the world. “Although this is a personal loss to us as Ndi Enugu, my heart, nevertheless, particularly goes out to his immediate household. On behalf of the Government and people of Enugu State, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, the Nollywood community, the Government and people of Anambra State, and all Nigerians and his global fans, who mourn this monumental loss,” he said. He prayed God to grant the bereaved family the strength to bear the loss and give the deceased eternal rest. “Your voice may have gone silent, but your legacy will speak for generations,” Mbah added.
